high.title: VN-Index Falls Below 1,800 Points — Experts Identify Oversold Stocks Expected to Rebound After Correction
high.summary:
The VN-Index has broken below the psychologically critical 1,800-point support level following a sustained period of sharp corrections, dragging major large-cap stocks significantly lower. According to Nguyen Anh Khoa, Head of Research at Agriseco, the correction has been primarily driven by investor caution amid geopolitical uncertainties, weak buying momentum in large-cap names, and persistent net foreign selling pressure. However, Khoa notes that the pullback is occurring on notably lower trading volumes — well below the 20-session average — suggesting that selling pressure is beginning to abate rather than accelerate. From a technical standpoint, several fundamentally sound stocks have entered oversold territory, presenting potential medium-to-long-term entry opportunities. For international fund managers, the breach of 1,800 is a key signal: sustained foreign net selling combined with weak domestic liquidity could imply continued capital outflows that may exert mild downward pressure on the VND. The next key levels to monitor are whether the VN-Index can reclaim 1,800 as support and whether foreign selling intensity diminishes in coming sessions.

---

high.title: Money Flowing into Stocks Hits Bottom — What Are Investors Waiting For?
high.summary: The VN-Index recorded its **third consecutive weekly decline**, falling 2.24% to close at **1,787 points**, while the VN30 index dropped nearly 2% to 1,931 points. Sentiment deteriorated sharply amid renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Breadth was decisively negative, with red dominating across nearly all sector groups — steel, technology, telecoms, industrial parks, banking, securities, and real estate all came under significant pressure. Notably, the Vingroup stock cluster (VHM, VIC), which had been a key market driver, weighed heavily on the index. Liquidity metrics are flashing a warning: money allocated to declining stocks outpaced that flowing into advancing stocks by a ratio of **2.13x**, and overall weekly trading volume deteriorated materially. For fund managers, the combination of three consecutive down weeks, a liquidity trough, and broad-based sector weakness suggests risk-off positioning is dominating. Key watchpoints: stabilization of geopolitical risk premium, any SBV liquidity support signaling, and whether the 1,787 level holds as near-term technical support.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Discusses Replacing the Banking Sector's Most Important Circular — Basel Capital Standards
high.summary: The **State Bank of Vietnam (SBV)** convened its **6th Steering Committee meeting on Basel capital standard implementation** on July 15 in Hanoi, chaired by Standing Deputy Governor Doan Thai Son, with participation from major credit institutions and the Big Four audit firms (KPMG, Deloitte, PwC, EY). The meeting reviewed progress from the 5th session and set out priority tasks to maintain the pace and quality of Basel adoption. This is a critical regulatory development: the eventual circular replacing the current framework will redefine **capital adequacy requirements** across Vietnamese banks, directly impacting their capacity to extend credit, manage risk-weighted assets, and distribute capital. For bond investors, tighter Basel-aligned capital buffers could affect bank demand for government bonds as high-quality liquid assets (HQLA). For equity investors, stricter capital rules may constrain near-term dividend payouts and loan growth at state-owned and private banks alike. Progress toward Basel III/IV compliance also signals Vietnam's continued effort to align with international banking standards, a positive longer-term signal for foreign capital inflows into the financial sector.

high.title: Vietcombank Chairman: Banks Lack Sufficient Capital to Fund Many Large Projects Ahead
high.summary:
Speaking at a Government Standing Committee conference chaired by the Prime Minister on July 18 — themed "Removing Bottlenecks, Unlocking Resources, Driving Growth" — Vietcombank Chairman Nguyen Thanh Tung outlined five critical challenges facing the banking sector. Most relevant to macro traders: **(1)** Banks face insufficient capital to meet rising credit demand from large infrastructure and public investment projects; **(2)** structural funding imbalances persist between short-term deposit liabilities and long-term lending requirements; **(3)** the cost of capital is expected to rise in the near term, pressuring net interest margins; **(4)** foreign currency supply constraints and exchange rate volatility remain a concern — a direct FX flag; and **(5)** collateral policy complications, particularly in localities undergoing urban rezoning, are impairing banks' ability to extend secured lending. For VND and bond traders, points 3 and 4 are most actionable: rising funding costs could push deposit rates higher, steepening the short end of the yield curve, while FX supply tightness signals potential SBV intervention pressure. Watch for any SBV response on credit room (room tín dụng) allocation and FX liquidity support measures.

---

high.title: VN-Index Plunges 44 Points — Experts Caution Investors on Key Risk
high.summary:
The Vietnamese equity market opened the new week with a broad-based sell-off, with the VN-Index shedding nearly 44 points (-2.46%) to close at approximately 1,743 points. Selling pressure emerged immediately at the open and was widespread, with close to 600 tickers declining, including large-cap names. Trading liquidity on HoSE remained subdued, with matched order value falling short of VND 18,000 billion — suggesting that dip-buying demand was insufficient to absorb the wave of selling.

Mirae Asset Vietnam's Head of Investment Advisory, Dang Van Cuong, flagged cautious signals, noting it is premature to confirm whether the market has entered a sustained downtrend or is experiencing a sharp corrective pullback. He emphasized that trend confirmation typically only comes in retrospect. Sentiment is described as "heavy," with the index still anchored in the 1,700-point zone.

high.title: Bank Deposit Rates – July 20: ACB Raises Rates Across 6-12 Month Tenors; Seven Banks Now Offering 7%+ on 12-Month Deposits
high.summary:
ACB made a notable upward adjustment to its online deposit rates on July 20, raising the 6-month tenor from 7.1% to **7.6% per annum**, the 9-month tenor from 7.2% to **7.7%**, and the 12-month tenor from 7.3% to **7.8%**. This puts ACB at the top of the deposit rate leaderboard among surveyed banks. Following this move, **seven banks** now offer 7% or above on 12-month deposits: ACB (7.8%), Saigonbank (7.2%), Bac A Bank (7.1%), and MBV, VCBNeo, VIB, and PGBank (all at 7.0% — PGBank having just raised from 6.9%).

Notably, the four state-owned commercial banks — **Agribank, BIDV, Vietcombank, and VietinBank** — have not adjusted their rates and continue to offer **6.8% per annum** on 12-month deposits, maintaining a meaningful spread versus private peers.

medium.title: Q2 2026 Financial Results Update (Morning of July 20): Banking and Securities Sectors Post Strong Growth, Hydropower Sector Lags
medium.summary:
Vietnam's banking sector is reporting robust Q2 2026 earnings, with VPBank (VPB) posting pre-tax profit of VND 10,959 billion — a striking 76% year-on-year surge — bringing H1 2026 cumulative profit to VND 18,880 billion (+68% YoY). TPBank (TPB) also delivered solid growth with Q2 pre-tax profit of VND 2,562 billion (+26% YoY). Strong banking profitability signals healthy credit expansion and improving net interest margins, which is broadly supportive of the sector's systemic stability. For bond and FX investors, robust bank earnings reduce near-term concerns around non-performing loan deterioration and suggest that monetary easing has not materially compressed bank profitability. This is a positive read-through for Vietnamese government bond demand, as well-capitalized banks remain key domestic buyers of sovereign debt. Watch for further earnings releases from state-owned banks (Vietcombank, BIDV, VietinBank) to assess the broader credit cycle trajectory.

---

medium.title: Approximately 80% of the Banking System's Mobilized Capital is Short-Term
medium.summary: At a Government conference on July 18 themed "Clearing Bottlenecks — Unlocking Resources — Driving Growth," SBV Governor **Pham Duc An** disclosed that approximately **80% of total mobilized capital across the banking system is short-term**, with medium- and long-term funding accounting for only ~20%. The Governor highlighted the structural mismatch between the dominance of short-term deposits and strong enterprise demand for medium-to-long-term credit, requiring credit institutions to carefully manage liquidity safety while supporting business access to capital. He also affirmed that the SBV has been conducting **proactive and flexible monetary policy** to stabilize the currency, control inflation, and support economic growth. This structural funding gap is a key systemic risk for Vietnamese banks and has direct implications for **interest rate dynamics**: heavy reliance on short-term deposits makes lending rates sensitive to deposit repricing cycles. For VND and bond traders, this disclosure reinforces why the SBV must carefully balance rate policy — any upward pressure on short-term deposit rates flows quickly through to lending costs and could dampen credit growth targets.

medium.title: Next Week is an Important Moment for Shareholders of Vietcombank, VietinBank, and BIDV
medium.summary: Vietnam's three largest listed state-owned banks — **BIDV, VietinBank, and Vietcombank** — will complete cash dividend record dates within a single week, with aggregate payouts exceeding **~10,500 billion VND (~$410M USD)**. BIDV sets its record date July 20 (paying 4.5%, ~3,276 billion VND on August 20); VietinBank and Vietcombank both set record dates July 24 (VietinBank paying ~3,495 billion VND, Vietcombank paying ~3,760 billion VND, both on August 27). For equity traders, the ex-dividend mechanics will create near-term technical pressure on bank share prices. More broadly, the scale of cash leaving these banks' equity bases is relevant to capital management and their ability to grow risk-weighted assets — a theme connecting directly to the Basel discussion above. The state's receipt of dividends (as majority shareholder) also represents a fiscal inflow worth monitoring for broader liquidity implications.

medium.title: Record-High Margin Lending Across Market Reaches Nearly VND 450,000 Billion — Multiple Brokers Cross the USD 1 Billion Threshold
medium.summary:
Total margin and advance lending outstanding across Vietnamese securities companies reached an estimated VND 445,000 billion (~USD 17.5 billion) at end-Q2 2026 — a record high — rising approximately VND 30,000 billion from end-Q1. Margin lending alone stood at VND 435,000 billion. Sixteen brokerages now carry loan books exceeding VND 10,000 billion, with five — TCBS, SSI, VPBankS, VPS, and HSC — surpassing the USD 1 billion mark individually. TCBS leads at over VND 51,500 billion. Notably, brokers backed by major bank parents (TCBS, VPBankS, LPBankS, MBS, SHS) drove the sharpest Q2 increases.

**Relevance:** Record margin balances at a time of a sharp equity market correction raises systemic risk concerns — forced margin calls could amplify downside volatility in Vietnamese equities and indirectly pressure the banking sector's asset quality. This is a key metric to monitor alongside the VN-Index trajectory.

medium.title: H1 2026 Bank Earnings Update (Morning of July 21): Three More Banks Report Profit Growth, Only One Sees a Decline
medium.summary:
The H1 2026 banking earnings season continues to skew positive. MSB reported pre-tax consolidated profit of over VND 3,400 billion for H1 2026, up nearly 8% year-on-year, with total assets exceeding VND 440,000 billion. Asset quality remained stable with a standalone NPL ratio of 1.64% (per Circular 31) and a consolidated NPL ratio of 1.83%. The loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) stood at 66.76% and the short-term funding for medium/long-term lending ratio (MTLT) at 26.89% — both within regulatory limits. PGBank also posted strong results, with net revenue up 13.8% YoY, fee income more than doubling, and pre-tax profit of VND 439.7 billion for H1 2026.

**Relevance:** Broad-based banking sector profit growth supports sector stability and underpins Vietnamese government bond demand. Controlled NPL ratios reduce near-term risk of credit stress, though the record margin lending environment warrants monitoring.

medium.title: Companies with Large Net Cash Positions (>50% of Market Cap) Flagged as Investment Targets in Rising Rate Environment
medium.summary: MBS Securities has published a strategy report identifying Vietnamese listed companies with net cash-to-market-cap ratios exceeding 50% as a distinct investment theme in the current rising interest rate environment. The brokerage argues that beyond benefiting directly from higher deposit income, cash-rich companies retain strategic optionality — they can pursue M&A, expand capacity, or launch new projects at attractive costs when liquidity-constrained competitors struggle. Some stocks in this universe are reportedly trading at market caps *below* their net cash holdings, implying deeply discounted valuations. For bond and FX traders, this report is a secondary signal worth monitoring: MBS's explicit reference to a "rising rate environment" as the strategic backdrop confirms that market participants are pricing in sustained higher interest rates in Vietnam. This has implications for VND liquidity conditions, corporate credit demand, and potentially the trajectory of SBV policy normalization. Investors should watch whether the SBV validates this rate expectation through upcoming open market operations or policy communications.

medium.title: BVBank (BVB) to List on HoSE This Week — 22nd Bank on the Exchange, H1 Profit Up 5x Year-on-Year
medium.summary: BVBank (Ban Viet Commercial Joint Stock Bank), founded in 1992 with over 33 years of operating history, will officially transfer its listing from the UPCoM market to the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (HoSE) on July 21, 2026. HoSE has approved the listing of approximately 641 million BVB shares at a reference price of VND 13,100/share with a ±20% trading band on the first day. BVB last traded on UPCoM at VND 13,300/share (closed July 9). The bank reports H1 2026 pre-tax profit up approximately 5x year-on-year, with charter capital of VND 6,408 billion and a network of 126 transaction points serving over 2 million customers. Management holds approximately 11% of the bank's capital. This is the third bank to list on HoSE in 2026, making BVBank the 22nd bank on the exchange. For equity investors, this is a direct VN-Index constituent addition — the wide ±20% opening band and elevated H1 profit growth could generate significant price discovery volatility on Day 1. The bank's strong profitability surge warrants scrutiny of the underlying drivers (NIM expansion, credit growth, or one-off items) given the broader rising rate narrative.

medium.title: Domestic Gold Prices Tumble Sharply in Afternoon Session of July 20 — SJC, PNJ, DOJI All Fall VND 1.5 Million/Tael
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices fell sharply in the afternoon session of July 20, 2026, with major retailers cutting prices by up to VND 1.5 million/tael (~$58/tael) across the board. SJC bar gold was quoted at VND 143–146 million/tael (buy–sell), down VND 1.5 million on both sides. Gold rings (vàng nhẫn) at SJC and PNJ also declined VND 1.5 million/tael to VND 141.5–145 million and VND 141–145 million/tael respectively. DOJI fell VND 1.3 million/tael to VND 142–146 million/tael. While gold market news is not a primary focus, significant domestic gold price moves are relevant for FX analysts as Vietnamese gold dynamics can influence USD demand (gold imports require USD) and informal FX flows. A sharp drop in domestic gold prices — if driven by falling international spot gold — reduces import pressure on USD, which is marginally supportive for the VND. Traders should monitor whether this price decline reflects a broader risk-off reversal in global gold or is a local supply/demand adjustment.
